paragraphs.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεόν, καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος.
paragraphs.translit: En archē ēn ho logos, kai ho logos ēn pros ton theon, kai theos ēn ho logos.

paragraphs.text: The same was in the beginning with God.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν θεόν.
paragraphs.translit: houtos ēn en archē pros ton theon.

paragraphs.text: All things were made through him; and without him was not anything made that hath been made.
paragraphs.original: πάντα διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ χωρὶς αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο οὐδὲ ἕν. ὃ γέγονεν
paragraphs.translit: panta diʼ autou egeneto, kai chōris autou egeneto oude hen. ho gegonen

paragraphs.text: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
paragraphs.original: ἐν αὐτῷ ζωὴ ἦν, καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἦν τὸ φῶς τῶν ἀνθρώπων·
paragraphs.translit: en autō zōē ēn, kai hē zōē ēn to phōs tōn anthrōpōn·

paragraphs.text: And the light shineth in the darkness; and the darkness apprehended it not.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸ φῶς ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ φαίνει, καὶ ἡ σκοτία αὐτὸ οὐ κατέλαβεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai to phōs en tē skotia phainei, kai hē skotia auto ou katelaben.

paragraphs.text: There came a man, sent from God, whose name was John.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο ἄνθρωπος ἀπεσταλμένος παρὰ θεοῦ, ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἰωάννης·
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto anthrōpos apestalmenos para theou, onoma autō Iōannēs·

paragraphs.text: The same came for witness, that he might bear witness of the light, that all might believe through him.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ἦλθεν εἰς μαρτυρίαν, ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός, ἵνα πάντες πιστεύσωσιν διʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: houtos ēlthen eis martyrian, hina martyrēsē peri tou phōtos, hina pantes pisteusōsin diʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: He was not the light, but [came] that he might bear witness of the light.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖνος τὸ φῶς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός.
paragraphs.translit: ouk ēn ekeinos to phōs, allʼ hina martyrēsē peri tou phōtos.

paragraphs.text: There was the true light, [even the light] which lighteth every man, coming into the world.
paragraphs.original: ἦν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
paragraphs.translit: ēn to phōs to alēthinon ho phōtizei panta anthrōpon erchomenon eis ton kosmon.

paragraphs.text: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world knew him not.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἦν, καὶ ὁ κόσμος διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ κόσμος αὐτὸν οὐκ ἔγνω.
paragraphs.translit: En tō kosmō ēn, kai ho kosmos diʼ autou egeneto, kai ho kosmos auton ouk egnō.

paragraphs.text: He came unto his own, and they that were his own received him not.
paragraphs.original: εἰς τὰ ἴδια ἦλθεν, καὶ οἱ ἴδιοι αὐτὸν οὐ παρέλαβον.
paragraphs.translit: eis ta idia ēlthen, kai hoi idioi auton ou parelabon.

paragraphs.text: But as many as received him, to them gave he the right to become children of God, [even] to them that believe on his name:
paragraphs.original: ὅσοι δὲ ἔλαβον αὐτόν, ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τέκνα θεοῦ γενέσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: hosoi de elabon auton, edōken autois exousian tekna theou genesthai, tois pisteuousin eis to onoma autou,

paragraphs.text: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
paragraphs.original: οἳ οὐκ ἐξ αἱμάτων οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος σαρκὸς οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος ἀνδρὸς ἀλλʼ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi ouk ex haimatōn oude ek thelēmatos sarkos oude ek thelēmatos andros allʼ ek theou egennēthēsan.

paragraphs.text: And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us (and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father), full of grace and truth.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας·
paragraphs.translit: Kai ho logos sarx egeneto kai eskēnōsen en hēmin, kai etheasametha tēn doxan autou, doxan hōs monogenous para patros, plērēs charitos kai alētheias·

paragraphs.text: John beareth witness of him, and crieth, saying, This was he of whom I said, He that cometh after me is become before me: for he was before me.
paragraphs.original: (Ἰωάννης μαρτυρεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ κέκραγεν λέγων· Οὗτος ἦν ὃν εἶπον· Ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·)
paragraphs.translit: (Iōannēs martyrei peri autou kai kekragen legōn· Houtos ēn hon eipon· Ho opisō mou erchomenos emprosthen mou gegonen, hoti prōtos mou ēn·)

paragraphs.text: For of his fulness we all received, and grace for grace.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐλάβομεν, καὶ χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος·
paragraphs.translit: hoti ek tou plērōmatos autou hēmeis pantes elabomen, kai charin anti charitos·

paragraphs.text: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ὁ νόμος διὰ Μωϋσέως ἐδόθη, ἡ χάρις καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐγένετο.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ho nomos dia Mōyseōs edothē, hē charis kai hē alētheia dia Iēsou Christou egeneto.

paragraphs.text: No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared [him].
paragraphs.original: θεὸν οὐδεὶς ἑώρακεν πώποτε· μονογενὴς θεὸς ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο.
paragraphs.translit: theon oudeis heōraken pōpote· monogenēs theos ho ōn eis ton kolpon tou patros ekeinos exēgēsato.

paragraphs.text: And this is the witness of John, when the Jews sent unto him from Jerusalem priests and Levites to ask him, Who art thou?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ Ἰωάννου ὅτε ἀπέστειλαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων ἱερεῖς καὶ Λευίτας ἵνα ἐρωτήσωσιν αὐτόν· Σὺ τίς εἶ;
paragraphs.translit: Kai hautē estin hē martyria tou Iōannou hote apesteilan hoi Ioudaioi ex Hierosolymōn hiereis kai Leuitas hina erōtēsōsin auton· Sy tis ei;

paragraphs.text: And he confessed, and denied not; and he confessed, I am not the Christ.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὡμολόγησεν καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσατο, καὶ ὡμολόγησεν ὅτι Ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ὁ χριστός.
paragraphs.translit: kai hōmologēsen kai ouk ērnēsato, kai hōmologēsen hoti Egō ouk eimi ho christos.

paragraphs.text: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elijah? And he saith, I am not. Art thou the prophet? And he answered, No.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτόν· Τί οὖν; σὺ Ἠλίας εἶ; καὶ λέγει· Οὐκ εἰμί. Ὁ προφήτης εἶ σύ; καὶ ἀπεκρίθη· Οὔ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ērōtēsan auton· Ti oun; sy Ēlias ei; kai legei· Ouk eimi. Ho prophētēs ei sy; kai apekrithē· Ou.

paragraphs.text: They said therefore unto him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?
paragraphs.original: εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ· Τίς εἶ; ἵνα ἀπόκρισιν δῶμεν τοῖς πέμψασιν ἡμᾶς· τί λέγεις περὶ σεαυτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: eipan oun autō· Tis ei; hina apokrisin dōmen tois pempsasin hēmas· ti legeis peri seautou;

paragraphs.text: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said Isaiah the prophet.
paragraphs.original: ἔφη· Ἐγὼ φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Εὐθύνατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, καθὼς εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας ὁ προφήτης.
paragraphs.translit: ephē· Egō phōnē boōntos en tē erēmō· Euthynate tēn hodon kyriou, kathōs eipen Ēsaias ho prophētēs.

paragraphs.text: And they had been sent from the Pharisees.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀπεσταλμένοι ἦσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων.
paragraphs.translit: Kai apestalmenoi ēsan ek tōn Pharisaiōn.

paragraphs.text: And they asked him, and said unto him, Why then baptizest thou, if thou art not the Christ, neither Elijah, neither the prophet?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν βαπτίζεις εἰ σὺ οὐκ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς οὐδὲ Ἠλίας οὐδὲ ὁ προφήτης;
paragraphs.translit: kai ērōtēsan auton kai eipan autō· Ti oun baptizeis ei sy ouk ei ho christos oude Ēlias oude ho prophētēs;

paragraphs.text: John answered them, saying, I baptize in water: in the midst of you standeth one whom ye know not,
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰωάννης λέγων· Ἐγὼ βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι· μέσος ὑμῶν ἕστηκεν ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε,
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autois ho Iōannēs legōn· Egō baptizō en hydati· mesos hymōn hestēken hon hymeis ouk oidate,

paragraphs.text: [even] he that cometh after me, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to unloose.
paragraphs.original: ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος ἵνα λύσω αὐτοῦ τὸν ἱμάντα τοῦ ὑποδήματος.
paragraphs.translit: ho opisō mou erchomenos, hou ouk eimi axios hina lysō autou ton himanta tou hypodēmatos.

paragraphs.text: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
paragraphs.original: ταῦτα ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐγένετο πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, ὅπου ἦν ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων.
paragraphs.translit: tauta en Bēthania egeneto peran tou Iordanou, hopou ēn ho Iōannēs baptizōn.

paragraphs.text: On the morrow he seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God, that taketh away the sin of the world!
paragraphs.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον βλέπει τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ λέγει· Ἴδε ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ αἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου.
paragraphs.translit: Tē epaurion blepei ton Iēsoun erchomenon pros auton, kai legei· Ide ho amnos tou theou ho airōn tēn hamartian tou kosmou.

paragraphs.text: This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man who is become before me: for he was before me.
paragraphs.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον· Ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεται ἀνὴρ ὃς ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·
paragraphs.translit: houtos estin hyper hou egō eipon· Opisō mou erchetai anēr hos emprosthen mou gegonen, hoti prōtos mou ēn·

paragraphs.text: And I knew him not; but that he should be made manifest to Israel, for this cause came I baptizing in water.
paragraphs.original: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τῷ Ἰσραὴλ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον ἐγὼ ἐν ὕδατι βαπτίζων.
paragraphs.translit: kagō ouk ēdein auton, allʼ hina phanerōthē tō Israēl dia touto ēlthon egō en hydati baptizōn.

paragraphs.text: And John bare witness, saying, I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove out of heaven; and it abode upon him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐμαρτύρησεν Ἰωάννης λέγων ὅτι Τεθέαμαι τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ὡς περιστερὰν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐπʼ αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: kai emartyrēsen Iōannēs legōn hoti Tetheamai to pneuma katabainon hōs peristeran ex ouranou, kai emeinen epʼ auton·

paragraphs.text: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize in water, he said unto me, Upon whomsoever thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and abiding upon him, the same is he that baptizeth in the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ὁ πέμψας με βαπτίζειν ἐν ὕδατι ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν· Ἐφʼ ὃν ἂν ἴδῃς τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον καὶ μένον ἐπʼ αὐτόν, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ·
paragraphs.translit: kagō ouk ēdein auton, allʼ ho pempsas me baptizein en hydati ekeinos moi eipen· Ephʼ hon an idēs to pneuma katabainon kai menon epʼ auton, houtos estin ho baptizōn en pneumati hagiō·

paragraphs.text: And I have seen, and have borne witness that this is the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: κἀγὼ ἑώρακα, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκα ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἐκλεκτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kagō heōraka, kai memartyrēka hoti houtos estin ho eklektos tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Again on the morrow John was standing, and two of his disciples;
paragraphs.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον πάλιν εἱστήκει ὁ Ἰωάννης καὶ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο,
paragraphs.translit: Tē epaurion palin heistēkei ho Iōannēs kai ek tōn mathētōn autou dyo,

paragraphs.text: and he looked upon Jesus as he walked, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God!
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐμβλέψας τῷ Ἰησοῦ περιπατοῦντι λέγει· Ἴδε ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai emblepsas tō Iēsou peripatounti legei· Ide ho amnos tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ δύο μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος καὶ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousan hoi dyo mathētai autou lalountos kai ēkolouthēsan tō Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus turned, and beheld them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? And they said unto him, Rabbi (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), where abideth thou?
paragraphs.original: στραφεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἀκολουθοῦντας λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ζητεῖτε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί (ὃ λέγεται μεθερμηνευόμενον Διδάσκαλε), ποῦ μένεις;
paragraphs.translit: strapheis de ho Iēsous kai theasamenos autous akolouthountas legei autois· Ti zēteite; hoi de eipan autō· Rhabbi (ho legetai methermēneuomenon Didaskale), pou meneis;

paragraphs.text: He saith unto them, Come, and ye shall see. They came therefore and saw where he abode; and they abode with him that day: it was about the tenth hour.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔρχεσθε καὶ ὄψεσθε. ἦλθαν οὖν καὶ εἶδαν ποῦ μένει, καὶ παρʼ αὐτῷ ἔμειναν τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην· ὥρα ἦν ὡς δεκάτη.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois· Erchesthe kai opsesthe. ēlthan oun kai eidan pou menei, kai parʼ autō emeinan tēn hēmeran ekeinēn· hōra ēn hōs dekatē.

paragraphs.text: One of the two that heard John [speak], and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter`s brother.
paragraphs.original: ἦν Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου εἷς ἐκ τῶν δύο τῶν ἀκουσάντων παρὰ Ἰωάννου καὶ ἀκολουθησάντων αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: ēn Andreas ho adelphos Simōnos Petrou heis ek tōn dyo tōn akousantōn para Iōannou kai akolouthēsantōn autō·

paragraphs.text: He findeth first his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messiah (which is, being interpreted, Christ).
paragraphs.original: εὑρίσκει οὗτος πρῶτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν ἴδιον Σίμωνα καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εὑρήκαμεν τὸν Μεσσίαν (ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον χριστός).
paragraphs.translit: heuriskei houtos prōton ton adelphon ton idion Simōna kai legei autō· Heurēkamen ton Messian (ho estin methermēneuomenon christos).

paragraphs.text: He brought him unto Jesus. Jesus looked upon him, and said, Thou art Simon the son of John: thou shalt be called Cephas (which is by interpretation, Peter).
paragraphs.original: ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν. ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ Σίμων ὁ υἱὸς Ἰωάννου, σὺ κληθήσῃ Κηφᾶς (ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Πέτρος).
paragraphs.translit: ēgagen auton pros ton Iēsoun. emblepsas autō ho Iēsous eipen· Sy ei Simōn ho hyios Iōannou, sy klēthēsē Kēphas (ho hermēneuetai Petros).

paragraphs.text: On the morrow he was minded to go forth into Galilee, and he findeth Philip: and Jesus saith unto him, Follow me.
paragraphs.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ἠθέλησεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν. καὶ εὑρίσκει Φίλιππον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: Tē epaurion ēthelēsen exelthein eis tēn Galilaian. kai heuriskei Philippon kai legei autō ho Iēsous· Akolouthei moi.

paragraphs.text: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδά, ἐκ τῆς πόλεως Ἀνδρέου καὶ Πέτρου.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de ho Philippos apo Bēthsaida, ek tēs poleōs Andreou kai Petrou.

paragraphs.text: Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, wrote, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.
paragraphs.original: εὑρίσκει Φίλιππος τὸν Ναθαναὴλ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὃν ἔγραψεν Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ καὶ οἱ προφῆται εὑρήκαμεν, Ἰησοῦν υἱὸν τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέτ.
paragraphs.translit: heuriskei Philippos ton Nathanaēl kai legei autō· Hon egrapsen Mōysēs en tō nomō kai hoi prophētai heurēkamen, Iēsoun hyion tou Iōsēph ton apo Nazaret.

paragraphs.text: And Nathanael said unto him, Can any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ· Ἐκ Ναζαρὲτ δύναταί τι ἀγαθὸν εἶναι; λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Φίλιππος· Ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō Nathanaēl· Ek Nazaret dynatai ti agathon einai; legei autō ho Philippos· Erchou kai ide.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!
paragraphs.original: εἶδεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Ναθαναὴλ ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει περὶ αὐτοῦ· Ἴδε ἀληθῶς Ἰσραηλίτης ἐν ᾧ δόλος οὐκ ἔστιν.
paragraphs.translit: eiden ho Iēsous ton Nathanaēl erchomenon pros auton kai legei peri autou· Ide alēthōs Israēlitēs en hō dolos ouk estin.

paragraphs.text: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ· Πόθεν με γινώσκεις; ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πρὸ τοῦ σε Φίλιππον φωνῆσαι ὄντα ὑπὸ τὴν συκῆν εἶδόν σε.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō Nathanaēl· Pothen me ginōskeis; apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen autō· Pro tou se Philippon phōnēsai onta hypo tēn sykēn eidon se.

paragraphs.text: Nathanael answered him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art King of Israel.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ· Ῥαββί, σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, σὺ βασιλεὺς εἶ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autō Nathanaēl· Rhabbi, sy ei ho hyios tou theou, sy basileus ei tou Israēl.

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee underneath the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι εἶπόν σοι ὅτι εἶδόν σε ὑποκάτω τῆς συκῆς πιστεύεις; μείζω τούτων ὄψῃ.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen autō· Hoti eipon soi hoti eidon se hypokatō tēs sykēs pisteueis; meizō toutōn opsē.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye shall see the heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὄψεσθε τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγότα καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autō· Amēn amēn legō hymin, opsesthe ton ouranon aneōgota kai tous angelous tou theou anabainontas kai katabainontas epi ton hyion tou anthrōpou.
